title: Cybersecurity Controls and Professional Conduct

header.html: 1.4 Understand cybersecurity controls: Technical controls; Administrative controls; Physical controls. 1.5 Maintain professional and ethical conduct: Professional code of conduct; Due care and due diligence; ISC2 Code of Ethics
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Three categories of controls

A control (also called a safeguard or countermeasure) reduces risk.

Category Also called Examples
Technical Logical Firewalls, encryption, access control lists, antivirus, multi-factor authentication, intrusion detection
Administrative Managerial or procedural Policies, procedures, training, background checks, risk assessments, change management
Physical Operational or environmental Locks, fences, guards, badges, cameras, fire suppression
Exam tip

. Ask what the control is made of. Software or hardware logic = technical. Rules and people processes = administrative. Things you can touch in the building = physical.

2Controls by function

Function Purpose Example
Preventive Stop the event Lock, firewall rule, least privilege
Deterrent Discourage the attempt Warning sign, visible camera, guard
Detective Find the event while or after it happens Log review, intrusion detection, motion sensor
Corrective Fix the damage and cause Patching, restoring from backup, quarantining malware
Recovery Return to normal operation Disaster recovery site, backup restore
Directive Tell people what to do Policy, procedure, signage
Compensating Replace a control that is not feasible Extra monitoring when a system cannot be patched

One control can have more than one function: a camera is detective and deterrent.

Exam tip

. Prevent before the event, detect during, correct after. A compensating control is an alternative that gives similar protection, not an extra layer.

3Professional conduct

Cybersecurity professionals have access and trust, so they must follow a professional code of conduct: act legally, honestly and in the interest of the public and the employer, keep skills current and protect confidential information.

Concept Meaning Example
Due care Doing the right thing: taking reasonable steps to protect assets, the way a prudent person would Applying patches, training staff
Due diligence Investigating and verifying before acting Checking a vendor's security before signing

Due diligence is the research; due care is the action. Failing at either can be negligence.

Exam tip

. Due diligence = think and check first. Due care = act and maintain. Remember "diligence = detective work".

4The ISC2 Code of Ethics

The Code has four mandatory canons. They are applied in order: a conflict is settled in favor of the earlier canon. Strict adherence is a condition of the credential; a violation can lead to peer-review action and revocation.

Canon Wording (short)
1 Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure
2 Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally
3 Provide diligent and competent service to principals (employers and clients)
4 Advance and protect the profession
Exam tip

. Society first, then the law and honor, then the employer, then the profession. If an employer asks for something that harms the public, canon 1 wins.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company installs security cameras at all entrances. In which category does this control belong?

  • APhysical, because it protects the building
  • BTechnical, because it uses electronic equipment
  • CAdministrative, because it follows a policy
  • DDirective, because it instructs the staff
Show the answer

Answer: A. Cameras at entrances are physical controls; they are detective and deterrent in function.

S2A firewall rule blocks all inbound traffic to a database server except from the application server. What type of control is this?

  • AAdministrative and detective
  • BPhysical and deterrent
  • CTechnical and corrective
  • DTechnical and preventive
Show the answer

Answer: D. A firewall rule is a technical control that stops the event, so it is preventive.

S3A system cannot be patched because the vendor no longer supports it, so the team adds extra monitoring and isolates it. What are these measures?

  • ADirective controls that instruct the staff
  • BCompensating controls that replace the missing patch
  • CDeterrent controls that discourage attackers
  • DRecovery controls that restore the system
Show the answer

Answer: B. When the primary control is not feasible, a compensating control gives similar protection.

S4Before signing a contract with a cloud provider, a manager reviews the provider's audit reports and security practices. Which concept does this describe?

  • ADue care, which means maintaining protection daily
  • BNon-repudiation, which means no denial
  • CSeparation of duties, which splits the work
  • DDue diligence, which means investigating first
Show the answer

Answer: D. Investigating and verifying before acting is due diligence.

S5A security professional is asked by an employer to hide a data breach that puts the public at risk. Which canon of the ISC2 Code of Ethics takes priority?

  • AProvide diligent service to principals
  • BAdvance and protect the profession
  • CFollow the instructions given by the employer
  • DProtect society, the common good and the infrastructure
Show the answer

Answer: D. The canons are applied in order, so protecting society comes before duty to the employer.

S6A written procedure for security staff that tells them how to respond to alerts is best described as which function?

  • ADirective, because it tells people what to do
  • BDetective, because it finds attacks
  • CCorrective, because it repairs systems
  • DPreventive, because it blocks traffic
Show the answer

Answer: A. Policies and procedures tell people what to do, which is the directive function.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Name the three control categories.

Show the answer

Technical, administrative and physical.

R2What is the difference between due care and due diligence?

Show the answer

Due diligence is investigating first; due care is acting to protect.

R3Which control function discourages an attempt?

Show the answer

Deterrent.

R4How many canons does the ISC2 Code of Ethics have?

Show the answer

Four.

R5Which canon comes first?

Show the answer

Protect society, the common good and the infrastructure.

R6What is a compensating control?

Show the answer

An alternative control used when the usual one is not feasible.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Categories technical (logical), administrative (managerial), physical
Functions preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, recovery, directive, compensating
Due diligence / due care check first / act and maintain
Code of Ethics four canons in order: society, honor and law, principals, profession
